description:
This map displays a Land Use / Land Cover (LULC) classification based on false-colour satellite imagery from Spot 5 (2.5 m resolution) acquired on 2011-07-10, covering an area near Novákpuszta, Hungary. The imagery source is CNES 2011©, distributed by Airbus DS/Spot Image.

The map shows distinct landscape features delineated by thin black lines into polygons, each labelled with a 4-digit classification code. Prominent linear features, consistent with the definition of "Lines of trees and scrub", are highlighted with thicker orange outlines.

The false-colour imagery renders dense, vigorous vegetation in deep red tones (e.g., areas labelled 3210), suggesting forest or dense woodland. Agricultural fields are visible as striped patterns of pink/red and green (e.g., the area labelled 2330, indicating complex cultivation patterns). A residential or built-up area appears in lighter grey/white tones adjacent to the striped fields. Other areas, such as those labelled 4100 and 4211, exhibit darker brown/red tones, potentially representing sparser vegetation, specific soil types, or riparian zones. The orange-outlined linear features represent strips of trees and scrub, visually separating different land use types, particularly between agricultural land and more natural vegetated areas.
